q: Acute Appendicitias: So what are the 3 majorcomplications + how do they occur + treated❓🍒
a:
1. Appendicular block

    → adhere to cecum,ileum, omentum (3days after onset) due to inflammation+fibrosis

    → AB-therapy→ regression

    → after 6w appendectomy

    → might develop into abcess or generalized peritonitis

  2. Appendicular abcess

    → transformed from appendic. block

    → AB + drainage (percut or surgical)

    → after 6w appendectomy

    → may develop into fistula (skin, bladder, peritoneum)

  3. Diffuse peritonitis

    → due to direct perforation, or abcess perforation

    → Appendectomy, peritoneal lavage, drainage + AB

q: What are the 3 severe consequence of peritoneal membrane contamination In secondary peritonitis ❓🍒
a:
1. immune-system activate + vasodilation (huge surface) + plasma-influx → fluid-sequestration into 3rd space → hypovolemic shock
  2. penetration pertoneal membrane → systemic circulation → sepsis + septico-toxic shock → multi-organ failure
  3. peritoneal irritation → bowel paresis → ↑fluid sequestration

q: Causes for paralytic ileus❓ (name at least 7)🍒
a:
💡
The 5 Ps: Peritonitis, Postoperative, low Potassium, oPioids, and Pelvic/spinal fractures
  1. Metabolic
    1. acidosis, uremia, ↓K, ↓Na
    2. Pelvic irradiation
    3. Neurologic (brain tumor, MS, etc.)
  2. Reflex
    1. post-operative *
    2. biliary +renal colic
    3. acute pancreatitis
    4. Sterile intraperitoneal fluid → onset of ascitis in cirrhosis, hemoperitoneum, chemical peritonitis
    5. acute fallopian torsion
    6. bladder distension
  3. Septic causes
    1. Localized/diffused purulent peritonitis
    2. Septic condition adjacent to peritoneal serosa

q: What do you do if PARESIS IS NOT RESOLVED CONSERVATIVELY in paralytic ileus❓🍒
a:
SURGERY

→ postoperative paresis → might have developed into mechanical obstruction (fibrinous adhesions resection)

→Septic focus generating intestinal paresis (localized peritonitis) → source -ectomie (i.e. appendectomy)

→ Peritonitis → Peritoneal drainage (+lavage)

→ if large distension → transient external -ostomie

q: What are complications of bowel obstruction if untreated❓(4)🍒
What can you do to detect fluid in the abdomen when eFAST doesnt confirm hemoperitoneum (not CT)❓🍒
a:
DIAGNOSTIC PERITONEAL LAVAGE

  • before: naso-gastric tube + urinary catheter
  • then catheter through needle → abdomen (subumbilically) → aspiration: >10ml fresh blood → positive hemoperitoneum
  • if negative (>10ml) → diagnostic peritoneal lavage → drained: >100.000 RBC OR bile/alimentary particles → positive hemoperitoneum
